claim_boundary: Eight assignments are analyst-reviewed from captured official PDFs and structured notes; claims are not independent reproductions.

rows.title: ReSepNet: A Unified-Light Model for Recursive Speech Separation with Unknown Speaker Count
rows.semantic_reasoning: Recursive separation makes the unknown speaker count part of the separation problem.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A recording may contain an unknown number of people speaking at once, but a useful separator must decide how many voices to return. Mechanism: ReSepNet applies a dual-path transformer repeatedly; each iteration estimates one source and cross-correlation decides whether another iteration is needed. It trains on two/three-speaker mixtures and tests on four/five. Result: The paper reports higher SI-SNR improvement than listed baselines and generalization from two/three-speaker training to four/five-speaker tests. Boundary: The evidence is synthetic WSJ0 mixtures, 8-kHz four-second windows, and a bounded count range; real rooms and end-to-end recognition are not tested. Results are author-reported.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Vocal-tract model with two directions: Static design for a dummy head and dynamic design for a speaking machine
rows.semantic_reasoning: Physical static and dynamic vocal-tract models expose how geometry and articulation shape sound.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A physical vocal-tract model should either hold a known shape still for teaching or change shape over time to demonstrate articulation. Mechanism: The static model fixes one tract configuration and radiates a repeatable vowel; the dynamic model uses blocks and cams to change simulated articulators and tract shape. Result: The paper demonstrates both models and argues that static and dynamic versions serve different education, phonetics, pathology, and technology purposes. Boundary: This is a two-page demonstration with no shared quantitative evaluation or claim of human-speech equivalence.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: LID Models are Actually Accent Classifiers: Implications and Solutions for LID on Accented Speech
rows.semantic_reasoning: Language identification must preserve language evidence while refusing the shortcut that treats accent as language.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A language-identification system should identify the language, not the speaker's accent or first language. Mechanism: The study compares ECAPA-TDNN, MMS, and GEO systems on several corpora, measures accent-language confusion, reverses chunks, and fuses acoustic and sequence representations. Result: Dutch-accented English is called Dutch in 82.6% of errors in one setting; sequence-aware systems reduce this confusion while retaining mainstream performance. Boundary: Datasets, accent categories, chunking, and aggregation define the result; it diagnoses a shortcut but does not prove cultural neutrality or universal transfer.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Pathology-Aware Speech Encoding and Data Augmentation for Dysarthric Speech Recognition
rows.semantic_reasoning: Pathology-aware representations and targeted data address systematic production differences rather than generic noise.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A recognizer trained on typical speech must understand speech altered by different medical conditions despite scarce labels. Mechanism: A BEST-RQ Conformer is continued on pathological speech; fine-tuning compares synthetic, out-of-domain, and transcript-embedding-selected data, with similarity losses. Result: The authors report 13.2% relative WER improvement from pathology-aware pre-training, up to 8.7% from synthetic data, 12.2% from OOD data, and 9.7% from semantic selection. Boundary: Etiologies, corpora, similarity model, and ratios bound the claim; improvements differ by condition and synthetic speech may not preserve clinical variation.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Fine-Tuning Text-to-Speech Diffusion Models Using Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback
rows.semantic_reasoning: Diffusion-loss-regularized reward optimization improves naturalness without letting TTS drift from learned speech structure.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: TTS must sound natural and intelligible while responding quickly enough for real use; diffusion refinement makes that balance difficult. Mechanism: DLPO fine-tunes WaveGrad 2 with a reward combining UTMOS naturalness and the original diffusion loss, comparing DPOK, KLinR, and diffusion-only optimization. Result: The paper reports gains over the baseline and competing reward objectives, with listeners preferring samples 67% of the time. Boundary: The evidence uses WaveGrad 2 and selected reward predictors; predicted metrics and pairwise preference do not establish broad real-time deployment.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: AC/DC: LLM-based Audio Comprehension via Dialogue Continuation
rows.semantic_reasoning: Dialogue continuation turns audio descriptions into answers grounded in the sound rather than fixed caption wording.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: An audio-language system should answer different questions about the same sound, not memorize one caption wording. Mechanism: An audio encoder feeds an adapter and language model; interleaved audio/text examples use token cross-entropy, with LoRA tested on AudioCaps, WavCaps, and Clotho. Result: Dialogue-continuation training enables zero-shot instruction following and improves reported AQA, while AAC gains are mixed. Boundary: Generated captions, benchmarks, and an LLM judge define the evidence; human usefulness for deaf or hard-of-hearing users is not established.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Beyond Attacks: Advancing Fake Speech Detection with Attack-Agnostic Methods
rows.semantic_reasoning: Attack-invariant representations test whether fake-speech detection survives changes in attack, codec, and language.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A fake-speech detector must recognize manipulation it has not seen, including changed codec, attack, and language. Mechanism: A frozen wav2vec2 front-end and AASIST backend produce embeddings; AIED suppresses attack variation and CSD projects into a shared subspace, tested on ASVspoof and IndicTTS. Result: The paper reports 4%, 12%, and 34% relative EER improvements on LA, DF, and IndicTTS, with ablations separating AIED and CSD. Boundary: Datasets, attacks, frozen front-end, and language coverage bound the result; IndicTTS EER remains high and no independent adversarial evaluation was performed.
rows.claim_boundary: Captured official PDF supports the structured note; results remain author-reported and were not independently reproduced.

rows.title: Continuous Learning for Children's ASR: Overcoming Catastrophic Forgetting with Elastic Weight Consolidation and Synaptic Intelligence
rows.semantic_reasoning: Importance-weighted continual learning protects earlier child-speech mappings while adapting to sequential speakers.
rows.evidence_excerpt: Problem: A child-focused ASR service may receive speech over time, but updating it can make it forget earlier speakers and require centralized storage. Mechanism: Whisper-small trains on ten sequential MyST batches. EWC adds an importance-weighted quadratic penalty; SI accumulates importance from parameter movement and loss reduction; models use no selection, rolling-window, or best-so-far selection. Result: EWC and SI keep WER more stable across ten batches and improve over ordinary sequential fine-tuning under the protocol. Boundary: The protocol is simulated from MyST, uses English child speech and Whisper-small, and treats parameter importance as a proxy rather than a privacy guarantee.
